subject: fix(interactive): never hold a session behind its own fork
instruction:
fix(interactive): never hold a session behind its own fork

`interactive.fork` ran the child's start inside the parent's coordinator, and a
start waits on provider readiness with `:infinity` — up to the ten-minute
readiness deadline. For that whole window the parent answered nothing: not
`info`, not `interrupt`, not its own turns. A user's live session could be
frozen behind a branch it does not own and cannot see.

Split along the line that matters. The coordinator now answers `{:fork_plan,
id}` with the child's start intent and `:count_fork` with a bump — both pure and
immediate — and `InteractiveSession.fork/2` starts the child outside it, on the
parent's own node, under the same 120s gateway ceiling `interactive.start`
already carries. A test pins the mechanism rather than the timing: a plan
creates no durable record and no coordinator, and the parent still answers
while a fork is in flight.

Two smaller hardenings found in the same read: `validate_configuration_options/3`
destructured `normalized_options/2` with a match, so an unreachable `:error`
would have crashed a live coordinator rather than refusing the call, and the new
`invalid_title` replies had been inserted between the pruned-cursor comment and
the clause it documents.

Acceptance. These tests are restored into the worktree after the session ends and must pass:
  - the coordinator plans a fork and starts nothing
  - the parent answers while a fork is in flight

Rules. Files that already exist under `test/` must not be modified or deleted — the change is graded against tests restored from the history after the session ends. New test files of your own are allowed and are left in place. Work only inside this worktree.
